h: פּוּרִים, מַאֲמָר ז׳ Purim — Maamar Zayin

p: and gladness, and joy and honor" (Esther 8:16).
The matter is that Yisrael are sanctified
from the root of the verse (Vayikra 11:44):
"You shall sanctify yourselves and be holy,
That is: the holiness of Yisrael
and this is what is said, "You shall sanctify yourselves."
And the holiness of the Avos,
from the root of the holiness of the Avos —
about this it is said, "and be holy,"
a state of holiness from the root.
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach.
Torah is from the awakening from below,
and it belongs only to Yisrael,
who engages in Torah is liable,
is the holiness rooted in the Avos,
and only Yisrael have a connection to it,
have the status of the uncircumcised,
which is not so for Yisrael:
even an uncircumcised one is in the category of circumcised
is from the holiness from Above,
which is fixed and established by Hashem Yisbarach,
that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you,"
and it too is exclusive to Yisrael,
as it is said (ibid. 16): "Between Me and
the Children of Yisrael it is a sign forever,"
and an idolater who keeps Shabbos is liable
וְקִיטְרוּגוֹ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ קְדוּשּׁוֹת הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל.
and his accusation is against the three holinesses mentioned above.
And this is what they said (Tanchuma, Ki Seitzei 10),
that he would cut off the circumcised members of Yisrael
This is the accusation against the sign of the covenant,
do not guard the holiness of the covenant
וְעַל כֵּן הֲוֵי לָךְ מַה שֶּׁבָּחַרְתָּ.
and therefore, "Here, take what You have chosen."
And Haman was of his seed,
about whom they said (Megillah 13b) that there is none who knows
we have already said that the intent is
and said, "They are asleep from the mitzvos,"
וְרַבָּנַן גַּם כֵּן עַם אֶחָד הֵן
and the Rabbis too are "one people" —
against the holiness of Yisrael from their own side,
and said that all of them,
are asleep from Torah and mitzvos.
And also against the holiness of time,
he said that they pass the whole year
with "today is Shabbos, today is Pesach"
as is expounded on what he said,
"And the King's laws they do not keep,"
for wherever "the King" is said unqualified
in the Megillah, it serves as both sacred and mundane
וְהַיְינוּ דְּקָאֵי עַל מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים
meaning that it refers to the King of kings,
the Holy One, blessed is He, as well.
And so it is written in the holy Zohar
עַל פָּסוּק בַּחֲצַר בֵּית הַמֶּלֶךְ וְגוֹ׳ [אֶסְתֵּר ה, א]
on the verse "In the court of the King's house," etc. (Esther 5:1):
this is the Holy One, blessed is He."
"And the King's laws they do not keep" —
that their intent is not for the sake of Heaven
in the rejoicing of the festivals,
but their intent is only for bodily pleasure,
for they are given to this
all the days of the year.
And regarding the holiness from the side of Hashem Yisbarach
he said: "He of Whom it is said
'Hashem is One' is asleep to His people"
on the verse "There is one people").
Who examines the hidden places of the heart,
knows that in truth Yisrael are sanctified
with all three holinesses mentioned above.
Therefore, after the miracle was revealed,
it is written, "The Jews had light" —
that is, the revelation of the holiness of Yisrael
from their own side, through the awakening from below,
that they engage in Torah and mitzvos,
"They accepted it anew in the days of Achashverosh."
And also the holiness of Yom Tov,
which is the holiness of time
along the lines of what they said (in Midrash Rabbah there):
The Holy One, blessed is He, said to him:
אַתָּה מַפִּיל עַיִן רָעָה בַּמּוֹעֲדִים שֶׁלָּהֶם
"You cast an evil eye upon their festivals?
I shall make you fall before them,
and they will add for themselves one festival
And although Yom Tov with a prohibition of melachah
they did not accept upon themselves,
nevertheless the rejoicing and the mitzvos
are at a time fixed by the month,
for they intercalate the months, etc.
for the holiness of Yisrael was revealed
from the side of being offspring of the Avos.
For Mordechai and Esther subdued them,
וְעַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (תַּנְחוּמָא תֵּצֵא י)
in line with what they said (Tanchuma, Ki Seitzei 10):
It is a tradition of aggadah
only by the hand of Rachel's children.
And it is stated (Pesikta, parshah 13, siman 4):
לִתְבּוֹעַ מִן זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל עֲמָלֵק וְכוּ׳
to exact payment from the seed of Amalek," etc.
That is because they are guarded
in the holiness of the covenant in essence
that is, the revelation of the holiness of Yisrael
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ו, א) וְרָאוּ וְגוֹ׳
as they said (Berachos 6a): "And they shall see," etc.,
"that the Name of Hashem is called upon you,
these are the tefillin of the head;
that is, that they are bound to the root
and as it actually was at the time of the miracle,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר [אֶסְתֵּר ט, ג] וְכָל שָׂרֵי הַמְּדִינוֹת וְגוֹ׳
as it is said (Esther 9:3): "And all the officials of the provinces," etc.,
for the fear of Mordechai had fallen upon them."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Yisrael Kedoshim 8 — “‘Oraisa, Yisrael and Kudsha Brich Hu are one’ are the three holinesses: Oraisa, what a person strives for through Torah; Yisrael, the holiness rooted in the Avos; Kudsha Brich Hu, His sanctifying them from Above.” Rav Tzadok there maps the same three-part verse onto Torah, Yisrael and Hashem, and adds that the holiness from Above rests on a person only in proportion to his preparation below.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 59a — “Rabbi Yochanan said: A gentile who occupies himself with Torah is liable to death, as it is said: 'Moshe commanded us the Torah, an inheritance'—it is our inheritance, not theirs.” The same discussion cites Rabbi Meir: a gentile who studies Torah is like a High Priest, and explains that statement as referring to the seven commandments incumbent upon them. The passage therefore distinguishes Israel's covenantal Torah inheritance from the study appropriate to the nations' own obligations; it does not exclude that study.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Purim 13 — “The holiness of the bris is fixed in Yisrael even without their deed … yet a person can recognize it only after first circumcising himself; then it is revealed retroactively.” The Radziner explains “sasson zo milah” from the same Nedarim 31b, and shows why an inherited holiness, rooted in the Avos, still needs the act that reveals it.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 58b — “Reish Lakish said: A gentile who establishes a cessation of labor is liable to death, as it is said: 'Day and night shall not cease.' ... Ravina said: Even on Monday.” The Gemara is discussing the creation of a religious day of cessation, extending its statement even beyond the seventh day. Rav Tzadok cites it as a sign of Shabbos's particular covenantal relation to Israel, alongside Torah and circumcision.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Maharsha, Chiddushei Aggados, Megillah 13b — “They expounded the superfluous word ‘one’: he told Him … ‘one people’—just as the other peoples are not in mitzvos, so the Rabbanan among them do not keep mitzvos.” Maharsha shows how the verse's extra words yield the charge, and so supplies the textual basis for Rav Tzadok's point that Haman denied the self-made holiness of even the talmidei chachamim.

paragraphs.text: Rashi, Megillah 13b, s.v. DeMafki LeShata — “They spend the year with shehi and pehi—'Today is Shabbos,' 'Today is Pesach,' and we are forbidden to work.” Rashi expands the Gemara's compressed expressions. The speech is Haman's hostile account of Israel's holy calendar, which Rav Tzadok interprets as an accusation against the sincerity of its festival service.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 5b — “Rabbah, Rava's son, said: Even if you say that it was on Purim itself, they accepted upon themselves the prohibitions of eulogy and fasting, but did not accept a prohibition of labor.” The discussion distinguishes Purim's festivity from the Torah festivals' prohibition of work. Rav Tzadok nevertheless sees its fixed date, rejoicing, and mitzvos as a revelation of the holiness of Israel's calendar.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 117b — “Shabbos is fixed and established; therefore, in both prayer and Kiddush, one says 'Who sanctifies Shabbos.' A festival, however, is fixed by Israel, for they intercalate the months and establish the years; therefore one says 'Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons.'” The source distinguishes the independently fixed seventh day from the calendar sanctity established through Israel. Rav Tzadok places Purim's dated observances on the latter side while treating the Divine sanctity of Shabbos as the third root.

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Seitzei 10 — “Rabbi Pinchas said in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman's name: It is a received aggadic tradition that Esav falls through Rachel's children, as it is said: 'Surely the youngest of the flock shall drag them away.' Why call them the youngest of the flock? Because they are the youngest of the tribes. Therefore Moshe said to Yehoshua, 'Choose men for us,' for he was of Yosef's tribe, concerning whom it is said, 'I fear God,' while concerning Esav it is written, 'He did not fear God.'” The continuation contrasts Yosef's restraint in forbidden relations and bloodshed with Esav's corruption in both. This provides the precise covenantal ground of the maamar's appeal to Rachel's sons.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I 153b, Vayeitzei — “Rachel gave birth to two righteous ones. ... Yosef and Binyamin are two righteous ones. Yosef merited to be the righteous one above because he guarded the covenantal sign; Binyamin is the righteous one below, so that the Shemittah is crowned between two righteous ones, Yosef the righteous and Binyamin the righteous. Was Binyamin righteous? Yes: all his days he did not sin against this covenantal sign, although he did not encounter an ordeal like Yosef's.” The Zohar explicitly grounds the status of both Rachel's sons in guarding the covenant. This is the specific contribution required by the maamar's explanation of why their descendants overcome Amalek.
